catalog_metadata.catalog_name: Event Radar North Bay Hiking Catalog
schema_notes: Coordinates identify the stated route start, not park centroids.
preferred_months, acceptable_months, and poor_months are climatological curation judgments, not access guarantees.
Weather sensitivities, seasonal fit, solo fit, scenic value, best time of day, and minimum daylight are derived recommendation attributes unless provenance says otherwise.
Dynamic closures, alerts, fire restrictions, reservations, and current trail conditions must be checked at recommendation time.
Parking prices are intentionally not frozen into records; notes describe the stable paid/free or reservation baseline.

hikes.name: Spring Lake Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Multiple park entrances have paid regional-park parking; neighborhood and connecting-trail approaches also exist.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: The official lake circuit is a mostly flat, paved, multi-use path. Expect walkers, runners, bicycles, and family use.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Generally an all-season option; runtime checks should still cover flooding, storm impacts, and park alerts.
hikes.important_route_notes: Use the official 2.3-mile lake circuit, not longer Spring Lake-to-Annadel combinations.

provenance.derivation_basis: The park calls the circuit mostly flat and paved; tree cover, lake-edge exposure, route length, and proximity to Santa Rosa support the recommendation attributes.
provenance.source_notes: The elevation figure is a conservative routing estimate rather than an agency-published statistic.

uncertainties: Exact elevation gain depends on entrance and GPS smoothing.

hikes.name: Canyon Trail to Spring Creek Trail Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Limited paid parking is available inside the Channel Drive entrance; legal roadside approaches may add distance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Multi-use state-park trail network; route-finding matters at several junctions.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Best after winter rains and in spring; summer heat reduces fit. Check park alerts after storms or fires.
hikes.important_route_notes: The record follows the exact official 7.4-mile loop, avoiding nearby 5.3- and 6-mile Annadel variants.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official route statistics and trail descriptions, supplemented by mapped vegetation and the park's exposed/open versus wooded segments.
provenance.source_notes: Distance and gain are for the named official route; do not merge with the park brochure's separate six-mile loop.

hikes.name: Taylor Mountain Summit Out-and-Back
hikes.park_or_area: Taylor Mountain Regional Park and Open Space Preserve
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park lot at Kawana Terrace; the lot can fill at popular times.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Steep, largely unshaded multi-use ranch-road and trail climbing from the city edge.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Strong cool-season choice; clay-rich open slopes can become muddy after rain and uncomfortable in summer heat.
hikes.important_route_notes: The agency describes about four miles round trip and 1,067 feet of climbing; junction choices can alter the exact trace.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official peak description, open grassland terrain, steep gain-per-mile, and exposed summit character.
provenance.source_notes: The official article uses approximate distance; minor route variants exist within the trail network.

uncertainties: Exact distance varies with summit-approach junctions.

hikes.name: Colgan Creek Loop
hikes.park_or_area: Taylor Mountain Regional Park and Open Space Preserve
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park lot at Kawana Terrace.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Gentler route using the lower eastern side of Taylor Mountain rather than the summit climb.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Broad seasonal utility, though the lower dirt trail remains rain- and mud-sensitive.
hikes.important_route_notes: This is intentionally a short lower-park loop, not a partial version of the summit route.

provenance.derivation_basis: Agency route feature on the newer lower trail, including distance, small gain, creek corridor, and oak/bay woodland.
provenance.source_notes: Use the agency-described loop; map releases should be checked during integration because this is a comparatively new route.

uncertainties: Trail naming and connector mapping are newer than the core park network.

hikes.name: Crane Creek Short Loop
hikes.region: Santa Rosa and Rohnert Park vicinity
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park lot at the single main entrance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Compact network of rolling dirt trails through open meadow and oak woodland.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Highest value in the green and wildflower seasons; avoid hot afternoons and saturated-trail periods.
hikes.important_route_notes: The park contains about 3.5 miles of trails; this record uses the agency's specific 1.4-mile sampler loop.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official short-loop itinerary plus open-meadow and oak-woodland descriptions.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is a map-derived estimate; the agency article does not publish gain.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Creekside to Big Leaf Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park parking at the main entrance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Multi-use dirt network with several signed junctions and a mix of woodland and open ridge.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool seasons favor the climb and greenery; clay-rich segments can be muddy after rain.
hikes.important_route_notes: Agency materials support the trail sequence; exact 3.8-mile/600-foot metrics come from a mapped secondary trace of that route.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official park route description and a secondary GPS route for exact metrics.
provenance.source_notes: Metric confidence is moderate because the land manager does not publish exact statistics for this named loop.

uncertainties: Distance and gain depend on the chosen connector sequence.

hikes.name: Alta Vista to Three Lakes Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park parking near the entrance; nearby street parking rules must be observed.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Compact multi-use park network with a sustained climb to Alta Vista and rolling lake connections.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Green-season and cool-day route; open slopes perform poorly in heat and after saturating rain.
hikes.important_route_notes: The agency describes the route as just under three miles with about 600 feet of climbing; the stored distance is rounded to 3.0 miles.

provenance.derivation_basis: Agency route article and park landscape description.
provenance.source_notes: Official distance is phrased as 'just under 3 miles'; 3.0 is a deliberate rounded representation.

uncertainties: Distance rounded from an official approximate statement.

hikes.name: Lake Trail at Riverfront Regional Park
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park lot at the main entrance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Broad, mostly level multi-use trail around the former gravel-pit lakes with a redwood grove connection.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Useful warm-weather fallback because of shade and low exertion; check for flooding after major Russian River storms.
hikes.important_route_notes: The official park page publishes 2.18 miles; another county article rounds the loop to 2.3 miles.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official route distance and description of lakes, redwood grove, and flat trail.
provenance.source_notes: The exact park page value (2.18) is retained; 2.3 is treated as a rounded secondary official value.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated; official county pages use both 2.18 and rounded 2.3 miles.

hikes.name: Ridge Trail and South Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park lot at Chileno Valley Road.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Short but hilly dirt loop across open hills; popular with hikers, runners, equestrians, and dog walkers.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Excellent green-season and golden-hour route; exposed slopes amplify heat, wind, and mud.
hikes.important_route_notes: The exact 1.9-mile combination is published by the land manager; elevation gain is not.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official route listing and park description of panoramic, rolling grassland hills.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is a conservative mapped estimate.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Bay View Vista Out-and-Back
hikes.trailhead_name: Tolay Lake Regional Park main trailhead
hikes.parking_notes: Paid regional-park parking at the park entrance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Long rolling ranch-road hike through open preserve lands to Bay and county views.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Most rewarding in cool, green months; exposure and clay soils sharply reduce hot- or wet-weather suitability.
hikes.important_route_notes: This is the 7.6-mile return route to Bay View Vista, not the park's shorter lake circuits.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official county peak itinerary and preserve landscape description.
provenance.source_notes: Agency metrics are approximate but route-specific.

hikes.name: Sonoma Overlook Trail with Upper Loop
hikes.managing_agency: City of Sonoma and Sonoma Overlook Trail Stewards
hikes.parking_notes: Small public access area near Mountain Cemetery; avoid cemetery-only or restricted spaces and follow posted rules.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Community-stewarded dirt trail rising directly above the City of Sonoma.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool mornings and green season are best; exposed slopes are poor in peak heat.
hikes.important_route_notes: The 2.4-mile figure includes the Upper Loop; the basic overlook out-and-back is shorter.

provenance.derivation_basis: Trail-steward route statistics and documented open hillside viewpoints.
provenance.source_notes: The steward site is the most route-specific authoritative source; it is not a state or county land-manager page.

hikes.name: North Sonoma Mountain Ridge Trail Out-and-Back
hikes.park_or_area: North Sonoma Mountain Regional Park and Open Space Preserve
hikes.route_end: Sonoma Mountain ridge near the preserve boundary
hikes.parking_notes: Small paid regional-park lot at the end of a narrow rural access road; arriving early reduces parking friction.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Sustained one-way climb of 3.8 miles through woodland and open ridge to nearly 2,000 feet.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool-season and spring route; summer climbing can be hot despite woodland segments.
hikes.important_route_notes: The agency publishes 3.8 miles and about three hours one way; 7.6 miles is the explicit return version. Gain comes from a route-specific secondary trace.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official one-way length/time and landscape description; elevation from a route-specific secondary map.
provenance.source_notes: The 1,140-foot gain is secondary; the agency does not publish a cumulative-gain statistic.

uncertainties: Cumulative gain is sourced secondarily.

hikes.name: Sonoma Ridge Trail
hikes.managing_agency: Jack London Park Partners for California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: Paid day-use parking at Jack London State Historic Park.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Long climb beginning in the historic Beauty Ranch area and continuing through shaded forest to the Sonoma Mountain ridge.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Shade extends its warm-season range, but long climbing still favors cool mornings; check storm and fire alerts.
hikes.important_route_notes: The route-specific park page gives 9.5 miles, 1,500 feet, and about four hours; the separate Sonoma Mountain Trail page describes another 8-plus-mile variant.

provenance.derivation_basis: Route-specific park-operator page states metrics and that there is more shade than sun.
provenance.source_notes: Do not substitute the park's distinct Sonoma Mountain Trail statistics.

hikes.name: Bald Mountain Loop
hikes.managing_agency: Team Sugarloaf for California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park day-use parking near the visitor center and campground.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Sustained mountain loop to a broad exposed summit, using a mix of single-track and fire roads.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Official route guidance describes 70–90 percent sun; prioritize cool days and early starts.
hikes.important_route_notes: Use the 6.6-mile loop entry, not the same page's 5.6-mile Bald Mountain out-and-back.

provenance.derivation_basis: Park-operator route table provides exact metrics, route, estimated time, and sun percentage.
provenance.source_notes: Metrics are route-specific and high confidence.

hikes.name: Pony Gate–Canyon Waterfall Loop
hikes.managing_agency: Team Sugarloaf for California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park day-use parking; this route uses the Canyon Trail area rather than only the main visitor-center start.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Short, steep-sided creek route with more than 100 steps on the Pony Gate portion.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Waterfall and creek payoff depends on recent rain; excessive rain can make footing and crossings unsuitable.
hikes.important_route_notes: The official route map identifies the two-mile/450-foot loop and stair count. It is a seasonal-water feature, not a guaranteed waterfall.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official park-operator route PDF and canyon/waterfall description.
provenance.source_notes: Trailhead coordinate is approximate within the Canyon Trail parking area.

uncertainties: Seasonal water presence is inherently variable.

hikes.name: Hood Mountain and Gunsight Rock via Pythian Road
hikes.park_or_area: Hood Mountain Regional Park and Open Space Preserve
hikes.parking_notes: Small paid upper lot reached by a steep, narrow park road; access and gate status require checking.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Very steep and sustained route with remote-feeling forest and ridge travel.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool, dry days are best. Heat, high fire danger, storm damage, and wet rock can materially change suitability.
hikes.important_route_notes: This record uses the agency's Pythian Road itinerary. Hood Mountain routes from Los Alamos Road or Sugarloaf are different hikes.

provenance.derivation_basis: County peak itinerary and official preserve description; conservative solo-fit judgment reflects length, gain, and remoteness, not a safety guarantee.
provenance.source_notes: Route-specific agency metrics are strong; exact cumulative gain may vary slightly by GPS.

hikes.name: Pioneer Nature Trail
hikes.route_end: Main grove features and picnic area
hikes.parking_notes: State Parks charges day-use vehicle parking at the entrance/main lot; fees can change, so runtime presentation should retrieve current pricing.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Flat, accessible main-grove path connecting the reserve's signature old-growth trees and interpretive features.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Strong year-round option and especially useful on warm inland days; storm damage and high-water alerts remain dynamic.
hikes.important_route_notes: The park page calls this an accessible, flat 1.5-mile round trip; a 1.7-mile variation continues to the picnic area and returns by road.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official accessible-trail description in a dense old-growth redwood grove.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is a near-flat estimate; the official route length is retained.

uncertainties: Exact gain is not agency-published.

hikes.name: East Ridge–Gilliam Creek–Pool Ridge Loop
hikes.park_or_area: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve and Austin Creek State Recreation Area
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park day-use parking at the reserve entrance/main lot.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Steep loop leaving the flat grove for forested ridges and the Austin Creek side of the park complex.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Shade makes it valuable in warmth, but steep forest trails become poor choices in heavy rain or immediately after damaging storms.
hikes.important_route_notes: The official hike list gives a 5.6-mile loop with a 1,100-foot climb; confirm the map and any connector closures before use.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official walk/hike list and topographic setting in dense redwood and mixed forest.
provenance.source_notes: The route traverses two connected park units; temporary connector closures are a runtime concern.

uncertainties: Route viability depends on connector status.

hikes.name: Bodega Head Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Free state-park coastal parking areas are typically available, but lots can fill on peak weekends.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Open bluff-top footpath with ocean, harbor, and headland views.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Good cool-weather alternative; strong wind, dense fog, and heavy rain are the main weather limiters.
hikes.important_route_notes: Stay on signed trails and back from unstable cliff edges. The state infosheet's 1.89 miles is more precise than common rounded two-mile descriptions.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official route length and open coastal-headland setting.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is map-derived and varies with minor bluff-spur choices.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Kortum Trail: Wright's Beach to Blind Beach Out-and-Back
hikes.parking_notes: State-park day-use parking at Wright's Beach; parking pressure and posted fees or restrictions should be checked.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Nearly continuous open bluff-top trail with several signed beach and roadside access points.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Broad seasonal use, with wind and rain more consequential than temperature. Spring brings wildflowers; summer fog is common.
hikes.important_route_notes: The 2026 state infosheet lists the Kortum Trail as 2.5 miles; this record explicitly doubles that named segment for a five-mile return route. Older brochure wording can imply a longer Wright's-to-Blind alignment, so integration should preserve the stated endpoints.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official 2.5-mile trail listing converted to a return route; elevation and suitability derive from mapped open-bluff terrain.
provenance.source_notes: Distance confidence is moderate because official publications do not describe route endpoints identically.

uncertainties: Official documents vary in how they describe the 2.5-mile Kortum segment and endpoints.

hikes.name: Pomo Canyon Trail from Shell Beach
hikes.parking_notes: Roadside state-park parking at Shell Beach is limited and can fill.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Steep trail connecting Shell Beach with the inland Pomo Canyon campground through coastal scrub, ridge, and forest.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool and dry conditions are best; forested soil and steep grades are poor immediately after heavy rain.
hikes.important_route_notes: California State Parks publishes 3.5 miles one way. This record is the explicit seven-mile return trip from Shell Beach, not a through-hike requiring a car shuttle.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official one-way distance and park map; elevation is a conservative map-derived round-trip estimate.
provenance.source_notes: The agency does not publish cumulative gain for the return route.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Salt Point Coastal Trail from Gerstle Cove
hikes.route_end: Salt Point coastal promontories north of Gerstle Cove
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park day-use parking at Gerstle Cove; facilities and cell service are limited.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Rugged bluff-top and rocky-shore route in a remote coastal park; stay well back from surf and cliffs.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Wind, fog, swell, and heavy rain dominate suitability; temperature is usually less limiting than inland heat.
hikes.important_route_notes: The exact three-mile sampler is secondary; the official park page validates the six-mile rugged coastline and landscape but not this route's precise metrics.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official landscape/access page combined with a reputable route guide for a defined Gerstle Cove coastal out-and-back.
provenance.source_notes: Route metrics are secondary and deliberately conservative.

uncertainties: Exact turnaround is descriptive rather than a named official endpoint; route metrics are secondary.

hikes.name: Pygmy Forest Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park parking near Woodside Campground; the inland trailhead is easy to miss without a park map.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Inland forest-and-prairie loop to a rare pygmy forest ecosystem and short interpretive boardwalk.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool coastal climate gives broad temperature fit; wet, poorly drained soils make recent rain a major suitability factor.
hikes.important_route_notes: Friends of Salt Point describes a 3.8-mile/two-hour route; Gaia maps a 3.1-mile/646-foot variant. This record keeps the longer route distance and flags the mismatch.

provenance.derivation_basis: State Parks validates the ecosystem; Friends of Salt Point and Gaia provide route variants and metrics.
provenance.source_notes: Distance and elevation originate from different documented variants and should not be treated as survey-grade.

uncertainties: Secondary sources describe 3.1- and 3.8-mile loop variants; 646 feet applies to the mapped 3.1-mile trace.

hikes.name: Rhododendron–Chinese Gulch–Phillips Gulch Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Small roadside reserve parking area on Kruse Ranch Road; no large visitor complex.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Short, steep forest loop in a remote reserve with limited facilities.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Rhododendron bloom is typically a spring feature, not a guarantee; winter storms and wet forest footing can reduce fit.
hikes.important_route_notes: State Parks lists the three trails at 2.12 miles total. The 400-foot gain comes from a secondary route description.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official trail-total and reserve ecology, supplemented by a secondary gain measurement.
provenance.source_notes: Seasonal bloom timing is generalized and must not be presented as current bloom status.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is secondary; bloom timing varies annually.

hikes.name: Coastal Prairie Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Free preserve parking at the gateway is limited; observe posted preserve hours and gate rules.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Open preserve trail climbing from Highway 1 into coastal prairie with broad river-mouth and ocean views.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Cool-season greenery and spring flowers add value; wind and saturated grassland soils are key constraints.
hikes.important_route_notes: The current official map labels Coastal Prairie Loop as four miles. It also labels Sea-to-Sky as 18 miles round trip, while an older map says 15; that longer route was excluded from the catalog.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official preserve map and landscape description.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation is map-derived. The four-mile current-map value is preferred over informal route totals.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Steep Ravine–Matt Davis Loop
hikes.parking_notes: Stinson Beach and town parking can be highly constrained on fair-weather weekends; start early and observe posted restrictions.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Classic steep loop with stairs, creek canyon, redwoods, exposed traverses, and a long descent.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Creek and waterfall are strongest in wetter months, but heavy rain makes stairs and roots hazardous; coastal fog may improve summer comfort.
hikes.important_route_notes: The route concept is documented by the Parks Conservancy; exact seven-mile/1,600-foot metrics come from a route-specific secondary guide. Trail closures or bridge/stair conditions require runtime verification.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official partner trail description plus a route-specific established hiking guide for metrics.
provenance.source_notes: Metrics are secondary; multiple direction/order variants produce small differences.

uncertainties: Exact loop distance and gain vary by Stinson connector and direction.

hikes.name: Cataract–High Marsh–Kent–Benstein Loop
hikes.managing_agency: Marin Water with One Tam partners
hikes.parking_notes: Limited roadside/trailhead parking near Rock Spring; Mount Tam road access can be slow and congested.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Steep, stair-like creek trail and forested watershed loop with many junctions.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Waterfall payoff follows rain, but do not recommend during dangerous downpours; dry-season flow can be minimal.
hikes.important_route_notes: One Tam publishes the exact 6.5-mile loop and moderate-to-difficult rating. Elevation gain is a map-derived catalog estimate.

provenance.derivation_basis: Official One Tam route and waterfall/creek description; terrain-based suitability judgments.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain should be verified against a canonical GPX before production import.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Ben Johnson–Dipsea Loop
hikes.park_or_area: Muir Woods National Monument and Mount Tamalpais State Park
hikes.managing_agency: National Park Service and California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: Parking or shuttle reservations are always required in advance for Muir Woods; entrance and transportation fees are separate and may change.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Popular old-growth start followed by a steep forest climb and descent across NPS/state-park boundaries.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: NPS lists a four-mile summer route and a five-mile winter route because the seasonal bridge is removed; runtime route selection must reflect bridge status.
hikes.important_route_notes: Store four miles as the standard warm-season loop. When the seasonal bridge is absent, the official winter alternative is five miles and should be treated as a route variant, not silently substituted.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS route card and access pages provide route metrics, seasonal variant, and reservation baseline.
provenance.source_notes: This is one of the catalog's clearest recurring seasonal route variations.

uncertainties: Official route is 4 miles in summer and 5 miles in winter when the seasonal bridge is removed.

hikes.name: Tennessee Valley Trail to Tennessee Beach
hikes.parking_notes: Free trailhead parking is limited and often fills on weekends; overflow walking may add distance.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Broad, mostly gentle valley trail, paved at first and natural-surface later, with a short final climb before the beach.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: NPS notes seasonal flooding can close the beach approach; fog and wind can change comfort quickly.
hikes.important_route_notes: NPS gives 1.75 miles one way; the stored 3.5 miles is the explicit return route.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS one-way route card and terrain/access warnings.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is a mapped approximation.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Tomales Point Trail
hikes.parking_notes: Free NPS trailhead parking at Pierce Point Ranch; the remote access road is slow and the lot can fill.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Long, treeless ridge walk through tule elk reserve country with no water or shade.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Wind, fog, rain, and limited daylight drive suitability. Wildlife-related closures or restrictions are runtime checks.
hikes.important_route_notes: NPS currently describes 9.7 miles round trip; its hiking guide rounds to 9.5. The final 1.7 miles are unmaintained, and NPS warns of bluff cracks and collapse near the point.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS destination page, official hiking guide, and current trail-advisory page.
provenance.source_notes: The catalog retains the more precise 9.7-mile NPS web value and records the 9.5-mile official-guide rounding.

uncertainties: Two NPS sources give 9.5 and 9.7 miles; gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Chimney Rock Trail
hikes.parking_notes: Free NPS parking at the Chimney Rock trailhead; seasonal visitor management or shuttle arrangements must be checked.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Short, open headland walk with ocean, Drakes Bay, wildlife, and spring-wildflower interest.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Strong winds and rain are primary constraints; wildlife protection or peak-season vehicle rules may recur.
hikes.important_route_notes: Stay far back from cliffs and obey wildlife closures. This is a short destination walk whose long drive is justified mainly by pairing with other Point Reyes activities.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS destination page and headland landscape.
provenance.source_notes: Elevation gain is a route-map estimate.

uncertainties: Elevation gain is estimated.

hikes.name: Abbotts Lagoon to Great Beach
hikes.parking_notes: Free NPS trailhead parking; weekend capacity is limited.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Gentle path through pasture and wetland to a lagoon, followed by softer sand to the ocean.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Wind, rain, seasonal wet areas, wildlife protections, and beach conditions should be checked at runtime.
hikes.important_route_notes: NPS describes Great Beach as about 1.5 miles from the trailhead, yielding a three-mile return trip. The lagoon edge alone is shorter.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS place page identifies the 1.5-mile route to Great Beach and the wetland/coastal environment.
provenance.source_notes: Earlier NPS planning material uses different wording for lagoon versus beach distance; the endpoint is explicit here.

uncertainties: Mileage differs depending on whether the turnaround is the lagoon, bridge, or ocean beach.

hikes.name: Alamere Falls via Wildcat Camp
hikes.route_end: Alamere Falls beach approach via Wildcat Camp
trail_sequence: beach route south to Alamere Falls
hikes.parking_notes: Free but limited NPS parking at Palomarin; the rough access road and weekend congestion add substantial friction.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Full-day coastal route with many junctions, remote sections, and a final beach approach whose safety depends on tides and surf.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Requires sufficient daylight and favorable tide/surf, wind, rain, and trail conditions; all are runtime checks.
hikes.important_route_notes: NPS says the safe route is at least 13 miles round trip via Wildcat Camp and warns against the unofficial cliff shortcut. Never recommend the shortcut. Beach access can be impassable at high tide or dangerous surf.

provenance.derivation_basis: NPS route warning and official south-district map; gain from a secondary route guide. Weak solo-fit reflects complexity and remoteness, not a safety determination.
provenance.source_notes: The distance is an NPS minimum. Elevation gain is secondary and varies by tracking method.

uncertainties: NPS calls 13 miles a minimum; beach conditions can change the practical route.

hikes.name: Coyote Peak Loop
hikes.managing_agency: Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District for California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: Paid state-park day-use parking near the entrance; current fee and lot status should be checked.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Forested state-park loop through Ritchey Canyon and a climb to Coyote Peak views.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: Shade broadens warm-weather use, but climbing still favors cool mornings; storms can affect creek and forest trails.
hikes.important_route_notes: Napa Outdoors describes a popular roughly five-mile loop. Its guide also uses 1,170 feet in connection with Coyote Peak, but that number may refer to summit elevation rather than cumulative gain; this catalog stores a rounded 1,000-foot estimate and flags it.

provenance.derivation_basis: State Parks landscape page and Napa park-district route guide; gain normalized conservatively due ambiguous labeling.
provenance.source_notes: This is the catalog's most uncertain elevation statistic and should be GPX-verified before production use.

uncertainties: Published 1,170-foot figure may be summit elevation rather than cumulative gain; stored gain is a curation estimate.

hikes.name: Mount St. Helena Summit Trail
hikes.managing_agency: Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District for California State Parks
hikes.parking_notes: No-fee, limited dirt-lot parking on Highway 29; roadside access and visibility make early arrival prudent.
hikes.access_baseline_notes: Five-mile climb each way, beginning on forest trail and continuing largely on exposed fire road to a telecommunications summit area.
hikes.seasonal_access_notes: California State Parks recommends spring and fall generally; summit wind, heat, winter snow/ice, fire restrictions, and closures require runtime checks.
hikes.important_route_notes: The official park page says five miles to the top, so the catalog stores ten miles round trip. A secondary trace reports 10.7 miles and 2,119 feet; distance is normalized to the agency's route statement while the secondary gain is retained.

provenance.derivation_basis: State Parks page and infosheet for route, terrain, access, and season; route-specific secondary trace for cumulative gain.
provenance.source_notes: Official distance (10 miles return) and secondary distance (10.7) differ. Old closure PDFs remain indexed; current status must come from the operating district at runtime.

uncertainties: Official round trip is 10 miles; secondary route is 10.7. Gain is secondary. Dynamic status must be checked because obsolete closure notices remain online.
